N362258  
July 1, 2026
  CLA-2-90:OT:RR:NC:N1:105  
CATEGORY: Classification  
TARIFF NO.: 9029.20.4080
  Woongchan Yum  Roberts & Kehagiaras LLP  2339 Commerce Street, Suite 162  Houston, TX 77002  RE:  The tariff classification of a heart rate monitor from Malaysia.  Dear Mr. Yum:  In your letter dated June 11, 2026, on behalf of your client, Interactive Health Technologies, LLC., you  requested a tariff classification ruling. Descriptive literature was provided for our review.  The merchandise under consideration is the IHT Spirit Heart Rate Monitor (Spirit HRM), a wrist-worn,  battery-powered, Bluetooth-enabled wireless wearable health device engineered to monitor and track  physical effort. This device features a secure, multi-component plastic housing comprising a top cover, a  bottom cover, a sealing rubber gasket, and an adjustable wrist strap, all designed within an IP-rated  waterproof enclosure for active use. Internally, its operation is managed by a Main Board containing a  Microcontroller Unit (MCU), control circuitry, a rechargeable internal battery, and a digital display screen.  Magnetic charger connectors are integrated into the lower casing for recharging.  The system incorporates an optical heart rate sensing module (OHR Board) that utilizes  photoplethysmography (PPG) technology. It emits light through a dedicated OHR lens via LED emitters into  the user’s skin, while photodiode sensors capture backscattered light signals to measure volumetric blood  changes. The device calculates and displays real-time physiological and operational metrics, including heart  rate (beats per minute), heart rate zone status, minimum/maximum heart rate, elapsed time in active zones,  activity goal progress, date/time, and battery depletion status. Wireless data transmission is facilitated by an  integrated Bluetooth module. System activation, long-term historical data logging, reporting, and group  metric management require pairing with a compatible host smart device running the proprietary Spirit  Software Suite, which includes classroom, assessment, and individual platforms. The unit does not support  cellular or standard smartphone notifications such as calls, emails, or text alerts.  In your letter you suggest classification within heading 8517, Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United  States (HTSUS). As described above, the device utilizes an incorporated optical heart rate sensing module  and imbedded software to calculate and display real-time physiological and operational metrics including 

heart rate (beats per minute), heart rate zone status, minimum/maximum heart rate, elapsed time in active  zones, activity goal progress, date/time, and battery depletion status. Additionally, this device uses Bluetooth  technology to wirelessly transmit that data to a tethered device for additional tracking functionality. Heading  8517, HTSUS, provides in relevant part for: “…other apparatus for the transmission or reception of voice,  images or other data, including apparatus for communication in a wired or wireless network (such as a local  or wide area network).” The item concerned is primarily used to monitor various aspects of a person’s  wellbeing. It incorporates sensors and a processing system that measures/calculates health related statistics. It  also has a secondary function of transmitting that data to a remote Bluetooth enabled device. Classification  under heading 8517, HTSUS, is precluded because the device concerned is a composite good (Section XVI  Note 3 and Chapter 90 Note 3) which execute the principal function of determining or calculating a  measurement. The ability to transmit that information to a remote device would be considered the unit’s  secondary or support function. As per the Explanatory Notes to heading 8517, carrier-current and other  transmitters and receivers which form a single unit with analogue or digital telemetering instruments or  apparatus…, are excluded from heading 8517. Additionally, measurement apparatus of Chapter 90 is  excluded from classification within Chapter 85. As such classification within heading 8517. HTSUS is not  applicable.   The applicable subheading for the heart rate monitor will be 9029.20.4080, HTSUS, which provides for  “Revolution counters, production counters, taximeters, odometers, pedometers and the like; speedometers  and tachometers, other than those of heading 9014 or 9015; stroboscopes; parts and accessories thereof:  Speedometers and tachometers; stroboscopes: Other speedometers and tachometers: Other.” The general rate  of duty will be free.  The duties cited above are current as of this ruling’s issuance.  Duty rates are provided for your convenience  and are subject to change. The text of the most recent HTSUS and the accompanying duty rates are provided  at https://hts.usitc.gov/.  This ruling does not address the applicability of any additional duties, taxes, fees, exactions and/or other  charges, which may apply to the goods discussed herein.  This includes, but is not limited to, tariffs and other  duties as provided for in Subchapter III to Chapter 99, HTSUS.  Thus, for example, in addition to the  classification stated above, the merchandise covered by this ruling may also need to be reported with either  the Chapter 99 provision under which an additional tariff applies or one of the Chapter 99 provisions  covering exceptions to such tariffs.  For further information to assist with the importation process, please refer to the frequently updated Cargo  Systems Messaging Service (CSMS) messages at   https://www.cbp.gov/trade/automated/cargo-systems-messaging-service and the Trade Remedies page at   https://www.cbp.gov/trade/programs-administration/trade-remedies.  The holding set forth above applies only to the specific factual situation and merchandise description as  identified in the ruling request.  This position is clearly set forth in Title 19, Code of Federal Regulations  (CFR), Section 177.9(b)(1).  This section states that a ruling letter is issued on the assumption that all of the  information furnished in the ruling letter, whether directly, by reference, or by implication, is accurate and  complete in every material respect.  In the event that the facts are modified in any way, or if the goods do not  conform to these facts at time of importation, you should bring this to the attention of U.S. Customs and  Border Protection (CBP) and submit a request for a new ruling in accordance with 19 CFR 177.2.   Additionally, we note that the material facts described in the foregoing ruling may be subject to periodic  verification by CBP.  This ruling is being issued under the provisions of Part 177 of the Customs and Border Protection  Regulations (19 C.F.R. 177). 

A copy of the ruling or the control number indicated above should be provided with the entry documents  filed at the time this merchandise is imported. If you have any questions regarding the ruling, please contact  National Import Specialist Jason Christie at jason.m.christie@cbp.dhs.gov.  
Sincerely,
  (for)  James P. Forkan  Director  National Commodity Specialist Division
subject: The tariff classification of a heart rate monitor from Malaysia.
